problems.label: Difficulty letting go and clutter that makes the home hard or unsafe to use
definitions: Keeps items of little use or value and becomes very upset when asked to part with them.
Has rooms that cannot be used for cooking, sleeping or sitting because of possessions.
Continues to bring in new items, through buying or collecting, despite a lack of space.
longTermGoals: The home is safe and the main rooms can be used again, and the client can decide about belongings with much less distress.

shortTermObjectives.text: Within 2 weeks, clear paths to all exits and the stove area, and keep them clear.
By session 3, describe in own words how the client would like to use each main room.
Complete at least 3 sorting practices of 15 minutes a week, rating distress at start and end.
For 4 weeks, log urges to buy or collect and resist at least half of them.
By week 12, make one main room usable for its purpose, as agreed with the client.
Complete the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intake and every 4 weeks; if low mood is high, discuss a medication evaluation.

collaborativeNote: Write goals and objectives with the client in their own words. Timelines and targets are examples to adapt; the client decides what matters, and the clinician checks safety and fit.
